newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-J.Jeans sees 65 pct pre-tax profit dip.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-J.Jeans sees 65 pct pre-tax profit dip.

text.p: Just Jeans Ltd said on Monday pre-tax profit would be 65 percent lower in the 1996/97 year to end-July than in the corresponding period a year earlier.

Just Jeans chairman Craig Kimberley said in a statement that although the company's future was strong, some poor merchandise decisions combined with exceptionally difficult apparel retailing conditions would cut profits for the year just ended. "Unfortunately the combined effect will be to reduce our pre-tax profit by some 65 percent in comparison with the record results we enjoyed last year," Kimberley said in a statement.
"I hasten to add that we are nevertheless very confident of the future. Our total sales volume has held up well, indeed our core jeans business has remained strong," Kimberley said.

"Our group stock levels have been reduced and we believe that we have cleared the decks of several potential problems and can turn our full attention to restoring margins to former levels in the coming financial year," Kimberley said.
"We look forward to a return to previous profitability levels in the future," he said.
Just Jeans reported net profit rose to A$14.11 million in the year to July 27, 1996, from A$12.65 million in 1994/95.
The group reported a 48.9 percent fall in net profit for the six months ended January 25, 1997.
Just Jeans shares were three cents up at A$1.62.
